title: Crows Decide Twice as Fast as Humans
summary: New research from the University of Tubingen in Germany found that crows can make visual decisions twice as quickly as humans and monkeys, and stay remarkably accurate while doing it. In the experiments, two carrion crows watched patterns of moving dots on a touchscreen. They had to work out whether most of the dots were moving left or right, then peck a target on the matching side. On average, the birds needed just 235 milliseconds to decide, less than a quarter of a second. Even when the direction was hard to tell, their choices were still better than random guessing, and with clear signals they were accurate nearly 100 percent of the time. Brain cells linked to each choice started acting differently just 70 milliseconds after the dots appeared. The researchers suggest the speed may come from the demands of a bird's life, since birds rely on vision for fast, precise moves in flight. Exactly how their differently built brains manage to decide so much faster is still unknown.
why_it_matters: It shows that animals can be surprisingly quick thinkers, which can help you notice how fast your own brain makes choices when you play games or catch a ball.
